details:
**Baha'u'llah**
The founder of the Baha'i Faith, born Mirza Husayn-Ali in Persia in 1817; his title means "Glory of God." A follower of the Bab, he was exiled from Persia and spent his final decades as a prisoner of the Ottomans, including many years in the prison city of Acre (Akka), where he died in 1892.

**Universal House of Justice in Haifa, Israel**
The supreme governing body of the Baha'i Faith, an elected institution located at the Baha'i World Centre on Mount Carmel in Haifa. National and local Spiritual Assemblies around the world are subordinate to it, and it has issued statements such as the letter "The Promise of World Peace" addressed to the peoples of the world.

**Book of Certitude (Kitab-i-Iqan)**
Baha'u'llah's chief doctrinal work, which explains progressive revelation: God has sent a series of messengers whose religions are stages of one unfolding faith, a doctrine sometimes called the unity of all religions. It includes the "Tablet of the True Seeker" passage describing how a seeker must become detached from everything but truth, and Shoghi Effendi translated it into English.

**The Seven Valleys**
A mystical, allegorical work by Baha'u'llah, written in answer to questions from Sufis, describing the soul's journey toward God through seven stages, such as Search and Love. The final valley is that "of True Poverty and Absolute Nothingness."

**Shoghi Effendi, the Guardian**
The grandson of Abdu'l-Baha and the first and only Guardian of the Baha'i Faith, who led it from 1921 until his death in 1957. He translated major texts into English, wrote the history "God Passes By," and launched the Ten Year Crusade.

**19 months of 19 days and the 19-day fast**
The Baha'i (Badi') calendar has 19 months of 19 days each, plus four or five intercalary days called Ayyam-i-Ha ("Days of Ha"), a time for gift-giving, hospitality and charity. They come just before the final month, 'Ala, during which Baha'is keep a 19-day sunrise-to-sunset fast.

**Manifestations of God**
The Baha'i term for the great messengers through whom God progressively reveals Himself, including Abraham, Krishna, Zoroaster, Buddha, Moses, Jesus, Muhammad, the Bab, and Baha'u'llah. Questions often list several of these figures as a giveaway.

**The Bab and Babism**
Siyyid Ali-Muhammad, "the Bab" ("the Gate"), founded the predecessor religion Babism in Persia in 1844, with eighteen early disciples called the Letters of the Living, and foretold "He whom God shall make manifest." At his 1850 execution by firing squad, the first volley famously failed to kill him and he briefly disappeared before he was shot again. His Declaration is commemorated on the evening of May 22–23.

**Ten Year Crusade and the Hands of the Cause**
A global teaching campaign from 1953 to 1963, launched by Shoghi Effendi, that greatly spread the faith worldwide. The Hands of the Cause of God are distinguished believers appointed to protect and spread the faith, including Martha Root, and they guided the faith after Shoghi Effendi's death until the Universal House of Justice was first elected in 1963.

**Garden of Ridvan**
The garden outside Baghdad where, in 1863, Baha'u'llah declared that he was the one foretold by the Bab. It is commemorated by the twelve-day Festival of Ridvan (April 21 to May 2), whose first, ninth, and twelfth days are holy days.

**Kitab-i-Aqdas**
The "Most Holy Book," Baha'u'llah's book of laws, written in Acre, which sets out practices such as obligatory prayer, the fast, and the calendar. It is often called the central or main text of the faith.

**Epistle to the Son of the Wolf**
Baha'u'llah's last major work, addressed to a hostile Muslim cleric, Aqa Najafi, the son of the cleric he called "the Wolf." It recalls the execution of the Nahri brothers, honored as the "King of Martyrs" and "Beloved of Martyrs" (the "twin shining lights"), whose deaths Baha'u'llah had also condemned in the Lawh-i-Burhan (Tablet of the Proof).

**Nine-pointed star, Lotus Temple, and Wilmette**
The nine-pointed star is the common symbol of the faith (nine stands for completeness), and another symbol is the "Ringstone" emblem. Baha'i Houses of Worship are nine-sided, notably the lotus-shaped Lotus Temple in New Delhi and the House of Worship in Wilmette, Illinois.

**Abdu'l-Baha**
Baha'u'llah's eldest son and successor, the second leader of the faith, who wrote "The Secret of Divine Civilization," the Tablets of the Divine Plan, and the Tablet to The Hague. His Will and Testament appointed Shoghi Effendi as Guardian and set up the faith's administrative order, including the institutions covered by the "Lesser Covenant" on succession.

**Gleanings and The Hidden Words**
"Gleanings from the Writings of Baha'u'llah" is a widely read anthology compiled by Shoghi Effendi from Baha'u'llah's huge body of writings; one passage compares religions to branches of one tree. The Hidden Words is a short book of ethical and mystical aphorisms by Baha'u'llah.
